evidence_search.notes: Current screen reads the repository-preserved source-attributed evidence and complete episode inventory. It does not claim fresh full-text access to every originating source. No canonical restamp or independent source verification is implied.

episode_inventory.purpose: Resolve the reported two-agent interaction into the shared-floor and arbitration invariants protected by FC-000056.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Sampled frames of the 93.5-second preserved video show one person holding two phones displaying voice interfaces in the same setting.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Visible device co-location does not establish exact spoken sequence or audio overlap.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Two voice assistants reportedly responded to the same human utterance. The assistants were running on separate devices while participating in the same human conversation.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The reported interaction collision concerns shared floor state, with device configuration and exact audio sequence remaining unverified.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The source reports two voice assistants responding to one human utterance without yielding in the same setting. The reported collision concerns shared conversational-floor coordination; individually functioning assistants can still interfere when turn ownership is not coordinated. Visual frames establish co-located devices but do not independently verify acoustic overlap or internal arbitration. Intentional, coordinated parallel output would be outside this diagnosis.

notes: Retain the historical confidence and source-attributed occurrence claim without upgrading to independent acoustic verification. The evidence does not demonstrate an internal missing coordination component or a product-wide promise of cross-device arbitration.

The unresolved intentional-parallel-design exclusion limits a definitive current-edition admission. Preserve canonical finding pending a playable full exchange and setup evidence; no fabricated transcript or inferred platform-wide defect. FC-044 describes reviewer evidence access separately, not the reported collision.

failure_recognition.condition: Two or more synthetic participants are participating in the same conversational context.
failure_recognition.assessment: The source reports two co-located voice sessions responding to a shared human prompt.

failure_recognition.condition: Coherent continuation requires coordination of speaker identity, active-turn state, turn completion, yielding, or next-speaker allocation.
failure_recognition.assessment: A single shared conversation requires turn allocation to avoid repeated competing replies.

failure_recognition.condition: One or more synthetic participants fail to recognise or act on the relevant shared turn state.
failure_recognition.assessment: The first-person account describes independent replies without yielding; this is an attributed behavioural inference, not inspected internal state.

failure_recognition.condition: The failure produces repeated answers, simultaneous or colliding responses, inappropriate interruption, inappropriate silence, or another material conversational-floor coordination breakdown.
failure_recognition.assessment: Repeated or colliding replies are reported in the bounded demonstration.

success_recognition.condition: Multiple synthetic participants share a conversational floor.
success_recognition.assessment: The source reports two co-located voice sessions responding to a shared human prompt.

success_recognition.condition: They use sufficient shared speaker and turn state for coherent allocation, yielding, handoff or bounded collision recovery.
success_recognition.assessment: The reported replies repeat or collide rather than demonstrate coordinated yielding.

success_recognition.condition: The observed exchange and coordination state demonstrate the intended turn ownership, including any explicitly agreed parallel participation.
success_recognition.assessment: No complete acoustic sequence or shared-state trace is available to independently confirm turn ownership.

exclusions.condition: A single synthetic participant gives an incorrect or irrelevant answer while turn allocation remains coherent.
exclusions.assessment: Multiple assistants, not one irrelevant answer, are described.

exclusions.condition: Ordinary network or inference latency delays a response without losing or corrupting turn state.
exclusions.assessment: Exact overlap and timing are unavailable; delay alone is not the claimed repeated-answer mechanism.

exclusions.condition: The primary failure is loss of prior conversational content or persona continuity rather than allocation of the current conversational floor.
exclusions.assessment: The reported defect concerns the current conversational floor rather than lost prior content.

exclusions.condition: Simultaneous output is intentional and supported by the interaction design.
exclusions.assessment: The full setup does not independently establish whether parallel participation was intended.

exclusions.condition: An authorised reviewer cannot access audiovisual evidence of an otherwise bounded event; evidence accessibility is classified separately.
exclusions.assessment: The occurrence claim is the human-observed collision; reviewer media inaccessibility is a separate evidence limit, not its alleged cause.
